speaker: dvm
text: Hello, this is Doctor Brennan. I've got Duke in the exam room with me now. I have you on speaker so I can examine him while we talk.

speaker: client
text: Great, thanks for calling. He's been limping on his back left leg since last Tuesday.

speaker: dvm
text: Did anything happen that day? A fall, or rough play?

speaker: client
text: He was chasing a squirrel at the park and he yelped when he turned. He held the leg up for a few minutes, then walked on it.

speaker: dvm
text: Has it been getting better, worse, or staying the same?

speaker: client
text: It was better over the weekend, but after our hike on Sunday it got worse again. He's toe touching in the mornings.

speaker: dvm
text: Have you given him anything for pain?

speaker: client
text: I gave him one of his old carprofen tablets, the seventy five milligram ones, on Monday morning. Just the one.

speaker: dvm
text: Okay, good to know. Nothing else? No aspirin or ibuprofen?

speaker: client
text: No, nothing else. He also gets a glucosamine chew every day.

speaker: dvm
text: Is he eating and drinking normally?

speaker: client
text: Yes, totally normal. He's still trying to jump on the couch, which I've been stopping.

speaker: dvm
text: Alright. He weighs thirty two kilos today. Temperature is thirty eight point six, heart rate ninety six.

speaker: dvm
text: Walking him in the hallway, he's a grade three out of five lame on the left hind. Standing, he shifts his weight off that leg.

speaker: dvm
text: On the left knee, there's some swelling on the inside, and I can feel a positive drawer and tibial thrust. The right knee feels stable.

speaker: dvm
text: His hips move freely without pain, and his toes and pads look fine.

speaker: client
text: What does the drawer mean?

speaker: dvm
text: It means the knee joint is loose. I'm most suspicious of a torn cranial cruciate ligament, which is like an ACL tear in people.

speaker: client
text: Oh no. My last dog had that. She had the TPLO surgery.

speaker: dvm
text: That's one of the options. I'd like to take x-rays of both knees today, under sedation, to confirm and plan.

speaker: client
text: Yes, go ahead with the x-rays. But please call me before doing anything else, I need to talk to my wife about surgery.

speaker: dvm
text: Of course. For now, no running, jumping, or stairs. Leash walks only, ten minutes at a time.

speaker: dvm
text: Since he had carprofen on Monday, I'll start meloxicam tomorrow morning instead, once a day with food, for fourteen days.

speaker: client
text: Okay. Strict rest, and the new anti-inflammatory starting tomorrow. Should I stop the glucosamine?

speaker: dvm
text: No, the glucosamine is fine to continue. I'll call you this afternoon after the x-rays.

speaker: client
text: Thank you. My number is the cell on file. I'll keep my phone on.
